basics.name: Saleh Abdelrahman
basics.label: Computer Engineering Candidate | Robotics and Computer Vision
basics.summary: Computer Engineering candidate specializing in 3D spatial perception, edge ML inference, and high-performance systems for autonomous robotics. Co-author on research presented at CVPR 2026, IROS 2026, ISPRS 2026, and MDPI Electronics.

work.name: Mission Control Space Services
work.position: Robotics Software Engineering Intern, AI & Autonomy Team
work.summary: Engineered computer vision and robotics software for space-grade embedded platforms.
highlights: Engineered a six-camera high-FOV imaging ring for ML-based 360-degree 3D reconstruction.
Trained and optimized quantized panoptic segmentation models, achieving 97% accuracy.
Built a multi-object tracking system that improved scientific sample selection speed by 60%.
Optimized stereo computer vision on ARM, achieving a 40x speedup.
Used profiling, multithreading, and parallel processing to reduce system latency by 50% and compute overhead by 84%.
Automated MLOps workflows with AWS S3 for data and model storage, reducing model cycle time by 90%.
Authored unit and integration tests in Python for customer-facing satellite applications.

work.name: NavINST, Royal Military College of Canada
work.summary: Developed calibration and data infrastructure for multi-sensor robotics systems.
highlights: Contributed to calibration of 15+ sensor platforms, including camera intrinsic and extrinsic validation.
Reduced LiDAR-camera reprojection error using intensity-based alignment algorithms.
Engineered automated translation and ingestion pipelines for city-scale multi-sensor datasets.

work.name: QUARRG Lab, Queen's University
work.summary: Developed robotics perception and control software for a Quanser QCar vehicle.
highlights: Engineered lane-following and obstacle-avoidance algorithms using Linux, ROS, and OpenCV.
Generalized computer vision pipelines to maintain control across diverse track layouts.

volunteer.summary: Oversee 13 AI research projects involving more than 50 students and lead academic outreach initiatives.
highlights: Guide project direction, collaboration, and alignment with researchers.
Strengthen relationships with faculty, researchers, and external research organizations.

volunteer.summary: Led AI/ML research for a 15-person robotics team competing in DJI RoboMaster competitions.
highlights: Contributed to three robots that secured first in Canada and fifth in North America.
Queen's University Major Access Award (2023-2028)
Undergraduate Student Research Award (2025)

projects.name: Pic2Plate Recipe Generator
projects.summary: Full-stack application that generates recipes from grocery images.
highlights: Developed backend API integrations, web scraping, and object classification.
Trained an 85%-accurate YOLO model to detect more than 50 grocery items.

projects.name: Uncertainty-Aware Segmentation for Adverse Weather
projects.summary: Computer vision research project using SAM/SAM2 for robust segmentation.
highlights: Improved segmentation performance by up to 49% IoU/Dice through uncertainty-aware fine-tuning.
Achieved 43% and 30% improvements in IoU and Dice using uncertainty-aware adapters.
